This seems like a reasonable compromise. I sort of wonder how many documents are losing this feature because they weren't in the top 5 languages. But I wouldn't block over it. I like the new tests.

@hackartisan I did some counting based on our language facets.
1. With this change, 2,032 records no longer have the enhanced qf field processing that used to.
2. Overall, there are 8,182 records that don't have this enhanced processing.
3. The 5 languages with qf fields cover 88% of the current records vs 91.5% before the change. 

Of course, these numbers will change as we ingest new content.

dpul-collections.title: Proposal: Adjust home page filters to have manuscripts & digital collections

comments.body: I'm not sure this is particularly user friendly. The button is called "digital collections" which is the name of the web site! I don't think it's obvious that clicking that will take a user to a list of "Collections". I think it's because we are conflating a traditional filter (type = poster) with something more general. Narrowing scope vs. showing which buckets all of our records are a part of. Although it's more work than a button, a new row, something like what northwestern does, makes much more sense to me: https://dc.library.northwestern.edu/
@eliotjordan I agree we need something better, this was just a quick stop-gap. I think I'm hearing your opinion is "it's better to have nothing there than this, given how confusing it is"?

What about a button to the left of "explore" that says "browse all collections"

similar to the wording of "browse collection" that's on the collection page
